picks.headline: First AI-driven telescope goes stargazing
picks.excerpt: Scientists from Northwestern, University of Chicago and Fermilab deployed a reinforcement-learning AI to autonomously schedule Dark Energy Camera observations, adapting the plan in real time as sky and weather conditions change -- a milestone toward self-running observatories, with performance the team rates comparable to a human scheduler.
picks.rationale: New milestone: a reinforcement-learning agent autonomously schedules a real survey telescope in real time -- a concrete step toward self-running observatories, AI directly advancing observational astronomy.

picks.headline: AI agent helps prepare synchrotron X-ray experimental measurements, paving the way for autonomous operation
picks.excerpt: Stanford and SLAC researchers built an AI agent that autonomously aligns crystal samples at synchrotron X-ray beamlines -- reading detector images, experiment logs and scan results, then issuing instrument-control commands -- a step toward self-driving experimental facilities that free scientists from routine setup.
picks.rationale: Distinct lab-automation advance: an AI agent reads instrument data and issues control commands to align samples at a major user facility, pushing beamline science toward autonomous operation.

picks.headline: AI 'brain age' from sleep EEG flags sharply higher dementia risk
picks.excerpt: UCSF researchers used machine learning on overnight sleep-EEG recordings from about 7,000 adults to estimate each person's 'brain age'; brains scoring older than the person's actual age were tied to a sharply elevated risk of developing dementia -- an AI biomarker turning routine sleep data into early neurological insight.
picks.rationale: Novel AI biomarker: machine learning on routine sleep-EEG estimates 'brain age' at scale (~7,000 adults) and links it to dementia risk -- AI intersecting neuroscience and clinical prediction, distinct from prior BCI/cognition coverage.
